assumptions: The first pilot is pre-sold and limited to one high-frequency closed loop before assets are purchased.
Washing and transport can be outsourced under service levels compatible with customer requirements.
The relevant packaging format is legally covered and technically reusable for enough cycles.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed anchor-lane commitment with deposits or minimum volume, audited trip economics including losses and repositioning, demonstrated return rates and utilization, outsourced service quotations, and asset payback under conservative conditions.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Reuse obligations require a physical circulation mechanism, and regional closed-loop density directly addresses reverse-logistics economics.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Covered shippers will need reusable systems and already pay packaging costs, but 2030 timing and willingness to rent from a new pool remain uncertain.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Recurring per-cycle revenue is understandable, but asset purchases precede revenue and depreciation, washing, repositioning, shrinkage, and low utilization can erase the assumed margin.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single dense regional closed loop is a disciplined beachhead, though eligible packaging interpretation and economically suitable lane volume are unverified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Local density and return history can build a strong lane position, but established pallet pools, 3PLs, and packaging suppliers possess scale and relationships.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Profitable lanes can support adjacent regions, packaging formats, tracking services, washing, and customer-owned asset management.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Asset density, operational data, and contracted routes can become defensible locally, but the assets are replaceable and contracts are currently hypothetical.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Outsourced closed-loop service could reduce customer complexity, but no cost, reliability, or compliance advantage over incumbents is quantified.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2030 mandate creates a credible planning tailwind, but near-term procurement urgency may still be limited.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Direct lane contracts and 3PL partnerships are logical but require enterprise selling, and the founder has no current shipper relationships or channel rights.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The pilot consumes the founder's stated capital ceiling and adds physical operations, working-capital exposure, loss risk, and partner coordination alongside full-time employment.

highest_value_structural_change: Require a multi-year take-or-pay anchor contract with customer deposits and loss allocation before purchasing any pool assets.
main_structural_strength: Dense closed-loop asset circulation can create recurring revenue and a locally compounding operational advantage tied to regulation.
primary_score_limiter: Capital intensity and reverse-logistics risk are poorly matched to the founder's budget and part-time constraint without contracted utilization.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The full 100,000 PLN budget funds only a narrow pilot, while reverse logistics and low utilization can eliminate margin and incumbents already possess scale.
